source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.7.1(c), including the proposition's preceding parameter convention
source_evidence.observation: For a random variable X and a positive parameter K3, property (c) is E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K3 lambda) for every lambda with 0 <= lambda <= 1/K3.
The exercise asks for an argument that the bound in property (c) cannot be extended to all lambda satisfying |lambda| <= 1/K3.

binders: A real-valued random variable X (PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1).
A positive real parameter K3 (PDF page 21; printed page 32, the parameter convention immediately before properties (a)-(e)).
hypotheses: The original property-(c) bound holds: E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K3 lambda) whenever 0 <= lambda <= 1/K3 (PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(c)).
conclusions: Show that this same property-(c) inequality is not valid in general after replacing its one-sided range 0 <= lambda <= 1/K3 by the symmetric range |lambda| <= 1/K3 (PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.4).

Equivalently, exhibit or justify an obstruction at an allowed negative lambda; for example, the admissible random variable X = 0 satisfies the original property for every K3 > 0, whereas at any lambda < 0 its left side is 1 and its right side exp(K3 lambda) is strictly less than 1 (derived directly from Proposition 2.7.1(c) on PDF page 21, printed page 32, and the extension requested in Exercise 2.7.4 on PDF page 22, printed page 33).
definitions_and_conventions: The MGF appearing in property (c) is the expectation E exp(lambda |X|), so the absolute value is applied to X and not to lambda (PDF page 21; printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1(c)).

The proposed extension changes the lambda-domain from 0 <= lambda <= 1/K3 to |lambda| <= 1/K3 while retaining the displayed bound exp(K3 lambda) (PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.4, referring back to property (c)).
implicit_context: The exercise inherits the context of Proposition 2.7.1, which concerns arbitrary random variables rather than only centered ones; centering is introduced only for the separate property (e) (PDF page 21; printed page 32).
The exercise concerns the exact bound in property (c), not the two-sided local MGF bound for X in property (e) (PDF pages 21-22; printed pages 32-33).

details: Property (c) permits only nonnegative lambda (PDF page 21; printed page 32).
The rejected extension would additionally include every lambda in [-1/K3, 0) (PDF page 22; printed page 33).
The phrase 'the bound in property c' retains both sides E exp(lambda |X|) and exp(K3 lambda); only the stated lambda range is enlarged (PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.4).

For K3 > 0 and lambda < 0, exp(K3 lambda) is strictly below 1, which makes the zero random variable an immediate counterexample to the proposed general extension (derived from the displayed property on PDF page 21, printed page 32).

Because the source proposition ranges over a general random variable X, one valid random variable satisfying the original property but violating the extended inequality is sufficient to establish the requested non-extendability (PDF pages 21-22; printed pages 32-33).

undebatable_constraints: K3 is positive, as required by Proposition 2.7.1's parameter convention (PDF page 21; printed page 32).
The absolute value remains on X inside E exp(lambda |X|); it is not moved to lambda or to the exponent as a whole (PDF page 21; printed page 32, property (c)).
The original domain is 0 <= lambda <= 1/K3, while the proposed extension is the full domain |lambda| <= 1/K3 (PDF pages 21-22; printed pages 32-33).

The proposed extension retains the same right-hand side exp(K3 lambda), rather than replacing it by exp(K3 |lambda|) or a quadratic expression (PDF page 22; printed page 33, 'the bound in property c').
No centering assumption may be silently added: Exercise 2.7.4 refers to property (c), while the source imposes E X = 0 only for property (e) (PDF page 21; printed page 32).

ambiguities.issue: The exercise says 'Argue' and does not prescribe a particular counterexample or proof format.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 22; printed page 33, Exercise 2.7.4, contains only the one-sentence request.
ambiguities.impact: Any mathematically valid obstruction to the universal extension is responsive; the degenerate example X = 0 is sufficient but is not uniquely required.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'can not be extended' leaves the failure quantifiers implicit.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 22; printed page 33 refers back to the universally quantified property-(c) inequality on PDF page 21; printed page 32.
ambiguities.impact: The natural contract is that no generally valid version of the same inequality holds for every random variable satisfying property (c) and every lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K3; it is not a claim that every individual nonzero distribution must fail for every negative lambda.

contracts.contract_plain_english: For a general random variable X and positive K3, property (c) bounds E exp(lambda |X|) by exp(K3 lambda) only for 0 <= lambda <= 1/K3. Exercise 2.7.4 asks why the identical inequality cannot be asserted on the symmetric interval |lambda| <= 1/K3. The newly included negative values make the right side less than 1. Taking X identically zero gives left side 1, so the original one-sided bound holds but the proposed negative-lambda extension fails.
